entities.name: PMID:25428725
observations: Observational study of 148 adults classified as early dilators (n=82), late dilators (n=37), or non-dilators (n=29) using brachial FMD measured at 50 seconds, 2 minutes, and 3 minutes after cuff release.
Late dilators had significantly higher blood viscosity; peak FMD did not differ significantly between early and late dilators (7.9 ± 4.3% vs 9.1 ± 5.7%).

Post-ischemia shear-stress area under the curve during the first 40 seconds was not significantly different among groups; age and blood viscosity, but not shear-stress magnitude, predicted FMD timing/pattern.

entities.name: Delayed FMD
observations: In the directly relevant human study, higher blood viscosity was associated with later brachial-artery dilation, whereas the measured early shear-stress stimulus was not associated with FMD timing/pattern.

entities.name: Blood viscosity
observations: Blood viscosity was significantly higher among late FMD dilators in a 148-person observational human study and independently predicted FMD timing/pattern.

entities.name: Shear stress
observations: Early post-ischemia shear-stress area under the curve was not significantly different among early, late, and non-dilator groups and was not associated with FMD pattern in the directly relevant study.
Other human studies show shear-stress stimulus influences peak FMD or changes dynamically during FMD, but do not establish a selective association with delayed FMD.
